text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert: gpu-serving group reporting repeated 'device address fault' and container crash loops (3 pods) in us-west-2. Alert rule: inference.cuda.illegal_address_rate > 0.5 for 5m. Paging @alex and @miguel. Incident channel created: #inc-1839123456

alex: oncall ack — jumping in. grabbing logs + coredumps now.

alex: quick snapshot from pod inference-worker-7f8b (node gpu-node-7):
```
[2026-03-15T10:02:11Z] ERROR runtime: cuda_illegal_memory_access: misaligned address at 0x7ff...
Stack: cuLaunchKernel -> implicit gemm_kernel -> load_tile -> illegal memory access
container exited with code 137 then OOM kill reported by kubelet
```

priya: noticed memory growth pattern correlated with longer context requests and streaming. Could be KV cache race under high-concurrency.

miguel: +1. Also seeing intermittent 'cuda: misaligned address' in dmesg on node. Suspect a kernel / driver-hotpath with our fused attention kernel.

caroline: customer impact — support dashboard shows ~4% increased errors for embed/streaming calls starting 10:00 UTC. Top customers: acme-ml, beta-saas. They're seeing 502s/timeouts, not data exfil. Inform CS.

alex: mitigation plan (quick): 1) take affected node out of rotation, 2) restart affected pods with fallback model (smaller variant), 3) disable prefetching cache feature to reduce KV contention. Doing step 1 now.

alex: running:
```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-node-7 && kubectl drain gpu-node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data -n prod
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/inference-worker --selector=pool=gpu,version=stable --timeout=5m
```

opsbot: drain job succeeded for gpu-node-7. Pods rescheduled to gpu-node-3/gpu-node-4.

miguel: after restart, one replica still threw illegal access during init. Rolling back driver-related flags might help. Proposing set env INFER_DISABLE_PREFETCH=true on deployment and pin model to quantized-small variant.

priya: can we also set CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 temporarily for the init phase to surface ordering issues? It will slow things but helps isolate race.

alex: applying patch: setting INFER_DISABLE_PREFETCH=true and model.fallback=quantized-small on canary (2 pods) first.

opsbot: canary pods are up (2/2). Metrics: error-rate down from 0.48 to 0.08 over 3m on canary.

caroline: notifying CS + account execs for acme-ml and beta-saas with ETA ~30m for full mitigation. Drafted message: "We're seeing transient GPU kernel faults affecting a subset of inference pods; we have mitigations in progress and are rolling fallbacks. No customer data impact. Updates every 15m."

miguel: good. Next steps: 1) roll the INFER_DISABLE_PREFETCH change to all GPU pools, 2) hold new model rollouts, 3) capture nvcrash and driver logs for root cause, 4) if recurrence, fallback to CPU-backed small worker for heavy customers.

alex: handing the incident to @miguel for night escalation and RCA. I'll remain on the channel for context. Handoff ts=1839123720.

miguel: taking over. currently scaling up quantized-small pool to absorb traffic and draining any node with repeated dmesg 'misaligned' lines. Creating follow-up ticket: INF-2248 (kernel-race-investigation).

opsbot: alert suppression set for 30m to avoid paging duplicates while mitigations roll.

caroline: noted — postmortem owners: miguel (lead), priya (runtime analysis), alex (mitigations/actions). Will schedule postmortem meeting and customer follow-up.

miguel: collecting core dumps + nvstack traces, will upload to S3 under s3://redwood-incidents/inc-1839123456/. If we confirm a driver/kernel bug we'll engage vendor support and consider pinned driver rollback.

alex: summary for runbook: immediate mitigations worked (disable prefetch + fallback model). Root cause TBD (likely kernel/attention-kernel race on concurrent KV access). Next: full roll, RCA, postmortem, vendor escalation if hardware/driver implicated.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged and assigned. Runtime status: mitigated -> partial (errors reduced). Keep channel updated. :white_check_mark:
